title: The Foundation of a Godly Marriage
subtitle: Proverbs 1:7
description: The Foundation of a Godly Marriage
reflectionPrompt: In what areas of our marriage have we been building on something other than the fear of the Lord? | When we disagree, do we instinctively turn to God's Word, or do we rely on our own reasoning and feelings? | How can we cultivate a deeper reverence for God together in our daily routine?
prayerFocus: Pray together that the fear of the Lord would be the governing principle of your marriage. Ask God to reveal any areas where you have built on sand rather than on the rock of His Word. Pray that your home would be a place where His name is honored above all.

title: Seeking Wisdom Together
subtitle: Proverbs 2:1-6
description: Seeking Wisdom Together
reflectionPrompt: Are we actively seeking God's wisdom together, or have we settled into spiritual complacency as a couple? | What is one specific area of our life where we need divine wisdom right now, and have we earnestly prayed for it? | How can we make the study of God's Word a more central and joyful part of our daily life together?
prayerFocus: Ask the Lord together to give you hearts that seek wisdom as for hidden treasure. Pray specifically for wisdom in whatever decisions or challenges you currently face. Thank God that He gives wisdom liberally and without reproach to those who ask.

title: Trusting God as a Couple
subtitle: Proverbs 3:5-6
description: Trusting God as a Couple
reflectionPrompt: In what area of our life together are we most tempted to lean on our own understanding rather than trusting God? | Can you share a time when God directed our path in a way we did not expect but later recognized as good? | How can we practically 'acknowledge Him in all our ways' this week?
prayerFocus: Surrender together the areas of your life where you have been leaning on your own understanding. Ask God to increase your trust in Him, and to direct your paths according to His perfect wisdom and unfailing love.

title: Guarding Your Hearts Together
subtitle: Proverbs 4:23
description: Guarding Your Hearts Together
reflectionPrompt: What influences in our life right now may be threatening the health of our hearts? | Is there anything in your heart — bitterness, fear, lust, discouragement — that you need to bring into the open today? | How can we better serve as watchmen for each other's hearts?
prayerFocus: Pray that God would search your hearts and reveal anything that is not pleasing to Him. Ask for the grace of diligence in guarding your hearts, and pray that the issues flowing from your hearts would bring life and blessing to your marriage and home.

title: Faithfulness in the Garden of Marriage
subtitle: Proverbs 5:15-19
description: Faithfulness in the Garden of Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Are we drinking deeply from our own cistern, or have we allowed our affections to become scattered? | What is one specific way I can better cultivate delight in my spouse this week? | Are there any threats to our exclusivity that we need to address honestly and urgently?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the gift of your spouse and ask Him to renew your delight in one another. Pray for protection against every form of unfaithfulness, and ask for grace to cultivate the garden of your marriage with tenderness and joy.

title: United in Teaching Your Children
subtitle: Proverbs 6:20-23
description: United in Teaching Your Children
reflectionPrompt: Are we truly united in how we instruct and discipline our children, or are there areas of significant disagreement? | What are we doing to ensure that God's Word is the foundation of our parental instruction? | How can we better support one another's authority and teaching in the eyes of our children?
prayerFocus: Pray for unity in your parenting and for the grace to be faithful teachers of God's truth. Ask the Lord to make His commandments a lamp and a light to your children through your consistent, loving instruction.

title: Treasuring Wisdom in Your Marriage
subtitle: Proverbs 7:1-4
description: Treasuring Wisdom in Your Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Is God's Word truly the 'apple of our eye' as a couple, or have other things taken that place of supreme value? | What would it look like to make wisdom a more intimate companion in our daily married life? | How does treasuring wisdom together protect our marriage from the temptations described later in Proverbs 7?
prayerFocus: Ask God to write His truth upon the tables of your hearts so deeply that it shapes every thought, word, and action. Pray that wisdom would be your most intimate companion as a couple, guarding you from every form of folly.

title: Choosing Wisdom Over Riches
subtitle: Proverbs 8:10-11
description: Choosing Wisdom Over Riches
reflectionPrompt: Honestly, does the pursuit of financial security sometimes take priority over spiritual growth in our marriage? | What is one financial decision we could make that would reflect our belief that wisdom is better than rubies? | How can we encourage one another to keep eternal values above temporal ones?
prayerFocus: Pray together that God would give you eyes to see the surpassing worth of His wisdom. Confess any areas where material pursuits have crowded out spiritual ones. Ask for the grace to order your finances and priorities according to His values.

title: The Beginning of Wisdom for Your Home
subtitle: Proverbs 9:10
description: The Beginning of Wisdom for Your Home
reflectionPrompt: How has our understanding of the fear of the Lord grown since we first married? | Are we growing in our knowledge of God Himself, or have we settled for merely knowing about Him? | What is one way we can deepen our shared knowledge of the Holy One this month?
prayerFocus: Ask God to deepen both your fear of Him and your knowledge of Him as a couple. Pray that your home would be a place where wisdom is not merely discussed but lived, where the Holy One is not merely acknowledged but intimately known.

title: Love That Covers
subtitle: Proverbs 10:12
description: Love That Covers
reflectionPrompt: Am I more inclined to stir up strife or to cover offenses with love in our marriage? | Is there a past hurt that I have claimed to forgive but continue to bring up or hold against my spouse? | How can we cultivate a culture of covering love in our home, where grace is the default response to failure?
prayerFocus: Ask the Lord to give you the kind of love that covers rather than exposes. Confess any areas where you have stirred up strife through unforgiveness or harsh words. Pray for the grace to reflect Christ's covering love in your marriage.

title: Seeking Counsel Together
subtitle: Proverbs 11:14
description: Seeking Counsel Together
reflectionPrompt: Do we have godly counsellors speaking into our marriage, or are we trying to navigate everything alone? | Is there a current challenge in our marriage where we would benefit from seeking wise counsel? | What holds us back from being more open about our marriage with trusted mentors, and how can we overcome that?
prayerFocus: Ask God to provide your marriage with wise counsellors: a faithful pastor, mature mentors, and honest friends. Pray for the humility to seek and receive counsel, and for discernment to know whose wisdom to trust.

title: The Crown of a Virtuous Spouse
subtitle: Proverbs 12:4
description: The Crown of a Virtuous Spouse
reflectionPrompt: In what specific ways am I being a crown to my spouse, and where might I be causing shame or discouragement? | How do I speak about my spouse to others — do my words honor them as a crown? | What is one area of personal virtue I can cultivate that would bless my marriage?
prayerFocus: Pray that God would make you a crown to your spouse: a source of honor, joy, and strength. Ask Him to reveal any ways you have been causing shame or discouragement, and give you grace to change.

title: Walking with the Wise Together
subtitle: Proverbs 13:20
description: Walking with the Wise Together
reflectionPrompt: Who are the closest friends in our life right now, and are they drawing us toward wisdom or away from it? | Is there a couple we admire for their godliness with whom we could cultivate a deeper friendship? | Have we noticed any negative influences from certain friendships on our marriage, and how should we respond?
prayerFocus: Ask God to bring wise companions into your life as a couple, and to give you discernment about the friendships that may be pulling you away from His purposes. Pray for the courage to invest in relationships that strengthen your faith and your marriage.

title: Building Your House
subtitle: Proverbs 14:1
description: Building Your House
reflectionPrompt: What am I currently building in our home, and is there anything I am tearing down, perhaps without realizing it? | What does our 'house' look like right now — is it marked more by construction or demolition? | What is one thing each of us can do this week to build up our home?
prayerFocus: Pray that God would make you wise builders of your home. Ask Him to reveal any areas where you have been tearing down with your own hands, and give you grace to construct a household that glorifies Him and shelters your family.

title: The Power of a Soft Answer
subtitle: Proverbs 15:1
description: The Power of a Soft Answer
reflectionPrompt: When we disagree, am I more inclined to give a soft answer or grievous words? What about my spouse? | Can you think of a recent conflict that was made worse by harsh words? How might a soft answer have changed the outcome? | What practical steps can we take to train ourselves toward soft answers in the heat of conflict?
prayerFocus: Pray for the Spirit's fruit of self-control in your speech. Ask God to put a guard over your mouths, that when anger rises, you would respond with grace rather than grievous words. Pray specifically for your next disagreement — that it would be marked by soft answers.

title: Committing Your Plans to the Lord
subtitle: Proverbs 16:3
description: Committing Your Plans to the Lord
reflectionPrompt: Are we in the habit of committing our plans to God together, or do we tend to plan independently and then pray? | Is there a specific plan or decision we need to roll onto the Lord right now? | How does committing our works to God change the way we respond when our plans don't work out?
prayerFocus: Take whatever plans, anxieties, and decisions are currently weighing on you and roll them together onto the Lord. Ask Him to establish your thoughts, give you clarity, and direct your steps according to His perfect will.

title: A Friend Who Loves at All Times
subtitle: Proverbs 17:17
description: A Friend Who Loves at All Times
reflectionPrompt: Am I truly a friend who loves at all times to my spouse, or does my love fluctuate with circumstances? | In what recent adversity did our friendship as a couple grow stronger or weaker? | How can we invest in the friendship dimension of our marriage this week?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the gift of friendship in your marriage, and ask Him to deepen it. Pray for the grace to love at all times, especially in the hard times. Ask that you would be to each other a brother or sister born for adversity.

title: The Gift of a Good Spouse
subtitle: Proverbs 18:22
description: The Gift of a Good Spouse
reflectionPrompt: Do I regularly thank God for my spouse, or have I allowed familiarity to diminish my gratitude? | When was the last time I told my spouse that I consider them a gift from God? | Reflecting on Henry's challenge: before I focus on how my spouse could improve, are there ways I need to grow?
prayerFocus: Spend time simply thanking God for each other. Name specific qualities, specific memories, specific ways your spouse has been a channel of God's favour in your life. Ask God to restore and deepen your gratitude for one another.

title: A Prudent Partner from the Lord
subtitle: Proverbs 19:14
description: A Prudent Partner from the Lord
reflectionPrompt: In what specific ways has God's gift of my spouse's prudence blessed our life together? | What areas of our life together most need greater prudence, and are we praying for it? | How does recognizing my spouse as God's gift change the way I view our differences and challenges?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the prudence He has already given your spouse, and ask Him to increase it. Pray for wisdom in specific areas of your life together. Ask God for the humility to see your spouse as His carefully chosen gift to you.

title: Walking in Integrity Together
subtitle: Proverbs 20:7
description: Walking in Integrity Together
reflectionPrompt: Is our marriage marked by integrity — consistency between what we profess and how we live at home? | What are our children learning from watching our marriage, and is that what we want them to learn? | Is there an area of our life where we have been living with a gap between our public profession and our private reality?
prayerFocus: Ask God for the grace of integrity: that your walk would match your talk, your home life would reflect your faith, and your children would be blessed by the consistency of your godly example. Confess any areas of hypocrisy and ask for renewal.

title: Building a Peaceful Home
subtitle: Proverbs 21:9, 19
description: Building a Peaceful Home
reflectionPrompt: Am I contributing to peace or contention in our home? What would my spouse honestly say? | Are there patterns of nagging, complaining, or picking fights that I need to repent of? | What would our home feel like if we both committed to active peacemaking this week?
prayerFocus: Ask God to reveal any contentiousness in your own heart and to replace it with a spirit of peace. Pray together for a home marked by tranquility, patience, and mutual respect. Ask for the humility to be peacemakers rather than peace-breakers.

title: Training Children in the Way
subtitle: Proverbs 22:6
description: Training Children in the Way
reflectionPrompt: Are we united in our approach to training our children, or do we contradict each other? | What is the 'way' we are actually training our children to walk, as revealed by our daily practices? | How well do we understand each child's unique temperament and needs, and how does that shape our training?
prayerFocus: Pray for wisdom and unity in training your children. Ask God to help you understand each child's unique design and to apply His truth faithfully to their lives. Pray for the long-term fruit of your training, trusting God with the results.

title: Hope Instead of Envy
subtitle: Proverbs 23:17-18
description: Hope Instead of Envy
reflectionPrompt: Are we envying any other couple or family, and how is that envy affecting our contentment? | How can we practice being 'in the fear of the LORD all the day long' in our daily married life? | What specific expectations and hopes do we hold onto together as believers?
prayerFocus: Confess any envy that has crept into your hearts and ask God to replace it with contentment and hope. Pray that the fear of the Lord would govern every hour of your day, and that your expectation in Christ would be the anchor of your marriage.

title: By Wisdom a House Is Built
subtitle: Proverbs 24:3-4
description: By Wisdom a House Is Built
reflectionPrompt: Which of the three — wisdom, understanding, or knowledge — does our household most need to grow in right now? | What are the 'riches' that currently fill the chambers of our home, and are they precious and pleasant? | What is one specific way we can apply wisdom to an area of our domestic life that has been neglected?
prayerFocus: Ask God to be the architect of your home, building it with His wisdom, establishing it with His understanding, and filling every room with the precious riches of His grace. Pray for a home that overflows with spiritual abundance.

title: Words Fitly Spoken
subtitle: Proverbs 25:11
description: Words Fitly Spoken
reflectionPrompt: When was the last time my spouse spoke a word to me that felt like 'apples of gold'? When did I last speak such a word to them? | Am I more often careless or careful with my words in our marriage? | What specific word of encouragement does my spouse need to hear from me today?
prayerFocus: Ask God to make your words to each other like apples of gold in settings of silver. Pray for wisdom in choosing what to say, patience in waiting for the right moment, and grace in delivering truth with love.

title: Putting Out the Fire of Gossip
subtitle: Proverbs 26:20
description: Putting Out the Fire of Gossip
reflectionPrompt: Have I been adding wood to any fires in our marriage by talking about our problems to the wrong people? | Is there someone in our lives who acts as a talebearer, fueling strife rather than peace? | Can we agree together on appropriate boundaries for how and with whom we discuss our marriage struggles?
prayerFocus: Ask God to guard your tongues from gossip and talebearing. Pray for the discipline to bring your frustrations to Him and to each other rather than to outsiders who will add fuel to the fire. Pray that where strife has been kindled, it may be extinguished by grace.

title: Iron Sharpens Iron
subtitle: Proverbs 27:17
description: Iron Sharpens Iron
reflectionPrompt: Do I welcome or resist my spouse's attempts to sharpen my character? | When I try to sharpen my spouse, is my motive and method loving and constructive, or harsh and critical? | In what area of character do I most need to be sharpened right now, and am I open to my spouse's help?
prayerFocus: Ask God for the humility to be sharpened by your spouse and the love to sharpen them well. Pray that the friction in your marriage would be constructive, not destructive, and that both of you would emerge sharper, holier, and more fit for God's purposes.

title: Confessing and Forsaking Sin Together
subtitle: Proverbs 28:13
description: Confessing and Forsaking Sin Together
reflectionPrompt: Is there any sin I have been covering rather than confessing in our marriage? | When my spouse confesses, do I respond with mercy or with punishment? | How can we create a safer environment for honest confession and genuine repentance in our relationship?
prayerFocus: Ask God for the courage to confess sin honestly and the grace to extend mercy generously. If there is anything hidden between you, bring it into the light before God and before each other, trusting in His promise of mercy.

title: A Shared Vision for Your Marriage
subtitle: Proverbs 29:18
description: A Shared Vision for Your Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Do we have a clear, shared vision for our marriage that is grounded in God's Word? | If we do not have such a vision, what steps can we take this week to begin developing one? | How has the absence of vision, or the presence of it, affected the direction of our marriage so far?
prayerFocus: Ask God to give your marriage a vision that is rooted in His Word. Pray for clarity about His purposes for your family, your ministry together, and your legacy. Ask for the discipline to keep His law and thereby find true happiness.

title: Trusting Every Word of God
subtitle: Proverbs 30:5
description: Trusting Every Word of God
reflectionPrompt: Are there any areas of our life where we are trusting our own judgment or cultural norms over God's pure Word? | How has God's Word served as a shield for our marriage in the past? | What is one passage of Scripture that we can commit to trusting together more deeply this month?
prayerFocus: Affirm together your trust in every word of God. Ask Him to be your shield as a couple, and pray for the faith to rest upon His Word when circumstances are uncertain and the world's counsel contradicts His truth.

title: Celebrating the Excellent Wife Together
subtitle: Proverbs 31:10-31
description: Celebrating the Excellent Wife Together
reflectionPrompt: Husband: What specific qualities in your wife can you praise today, following the example of the Proverbs 31 husband? | Wife: Which qualities of the Proverbs 31 woman do you most aspire to grow in, and how can your husband support that growth? | As we finish this month in Proverbs, what is the most important lesson we have learned together, and how will we carry it forward?
prayerFocus: Spend time praising God together for the gift of your marriage. Thank Him for what He has taught you through Proverbs this month. Ask Him to continue building your home on the fear of the Lord, that your marriage may be a testimony to His grace for generations to come.

title: Called Together as Saints
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 1
description: Called Together as Saints
reflectionPrompt: What do you believe God's specific calling is for your marriage? Have you ever discussed this together? | How does knowing you are 'beloved of God' change the way you treat each other daily? | In what areas of your marriage do you most need God's grace and peace right now?
prayerFocus: Pray together that God would reveal the specific calling He has for your marriage. Ask Him to fill your home with grace and peace. Commit this month of study in Romans to the Lord, asking Him to transform your marriage through His Word.

title: Not Ashamed of the Gospel
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 2
description: Not Ashamed of the Gospel
reflectionPrompt: In what ways might we be living a 'functionally secular' marriage — where faith is an add-on rather than the foundation? | How does the Gospel specifically help you forgive your spouse when they have hurt you? | What would it look like for our home to be a place where the Gospel is not just believed but visibly lived?
prayerFocus: Pray that the Gospel would move from a Sunday truth to a daily reality in your marriage. Ask God to make you bold and unashamed in living out your faith together, and to give you power through the Gospel for every challenge you face.

title: Kindness That Leads to Change
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 3
description: Kindness That Leads to Change
reflectionPrompt: In what areas are you most tempted to judge your spouse? How might you show kindness instead? | Have you experienced God's kindness leading you to repentance in your own life? How can you extend that same kindness? | What would change in your marriage if both of you committed to leading with grace rather than criticism?
prayerFocus: Confess any patterns of judgment in your marriage. Ask God to replace a critical spirit with His kindness, forbearance, and longsuffering. Pray that your home would be a place where grace — not condemnation — leads to genuine change.

title: Heart Transformation Over Outward Show
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 4
description: Heart Transformation Over Outward Show
reflectionPrompt: Is there an area where our marriage looks good on the outside but needs work on the inside? | How can we cultivate genuine heart transformation rather than just outward religious behavior? | What would it look like for our marriage to seek God's praise rather than the praise of people?
prayerFocus: Pray for authentic hearts. Ask God to search your marriage and reveal any areas of pretense or performance. Invite the Holy Spirit to do a deep, inward work that transforms your love from the inside out.

title: Both Sinners, Both Saved by Grace
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 5
description: Both Sinners, Both Saved by Grace
reflectionPrompt: Do you tend to keep score in your marriage — tracking who does more, gives more, or sacrifices more? How does Romans 3:23 challenge this? | How does knowing that you are both sinners saved by grace change the way you handle conflict? | What would it look like to extend 'free justification' to your spouse — forgiving without requiring them to earn it?
prayerFocus: Thank God together for the gift of justification by grace. Confess any patterns of scorekeeping or self-righteousness in your marriage. Ask God to help you extend the same free grace to each other that He has lavished upon you through Christ.

title: Justified by Faith, Not Performance
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 6
description: Justified by Faith, Not Performance
reflectionPrompt: Is our marriage more 'law-based' (performance earns acceptance) or 'grace-based' (acceptance is unconditional)? Be honest. | In what areas do you feel pressure to perform in order to be loved? How does the Gospel free you from that pressure? | How can you show your spouse this week that your love is not contingent on their performance?
prayerFocus: Pray that your marriage would be built on grace, not performance. Ask God to free you both from the burden of earning each other's love and to anchor your acceptance in the Gospel, where love is given freely through faith.

title: Against Hope, Believed in Hope
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 7
description: Against Hope, Believed in Hope
reflectionPrompt: Where in your marriage do you need to believe 'against hope'? What seems impossible right now? | Abraham refused to let his limitations define reality. What limitations are you allowing to define your marriage? | What does it mean to be 'fully persuaded' that God is able to transform your marriage?
prayerFocus: Bring the impossible areas of your marriage before God tonight. Like Abraham, refuse to stagger at God's promises through unbelief. Ask God to strengthen your faith and to do what only He can do in your relationship.

title: Fully Persuaded Together
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 8
description: Fully Persuaded Together
reflectionPrompt: Would you describe your faith as a couple as 'settled' or 'wavering'? What causes it to waver? | How does trusting God together glorify Him in a way that trusting individually cannot? | What promise of God do you most need to be 'fully persuaded' about for your marriage right now?
prayerFocus: Declare together that God is able. Pray over the specific areas where your faith has wavered. Ask the Holy Spirit to strengthen your shared conviction and to give glory to God through your trust.

title: Peace with God, Peace with Each Other
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 9
description: Peace with God, Peace with Each Other
reflectionPrompt: How does your individual peace with God affect the peace in your marriage? | Can you identify the tribulation-patience-character-hope progression in your marriage journey? | In what specific way has God's love been 'shed abroad' in your heart recently? How can you pour that love toward your spouse?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the peace that comes through justification. Ask Him to deepen your individual walks with Him so that peace flows naturally into your marriage. Pray through the progression: embrace the tribulation, ask for patience, trust the process, and hold onto hope.

title: Loving When Your Spouse Falls Short
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 10
description: Loving When Your Spouse Falls Short
reflectionPrompt: When your spouse falls short, is your first instinct to love or to withdraw? Why? | How does remembering that God loved you 'while you were yet a sinner' change the way you love your spouse? | What would it look like to demonstrate your love most clearly during your spouse's worst moments rather than their best?
prayerFocus: Ask God to pour His unconditional love into your hearts so that you can love each other the way He loves you — not based on performance, but based on commitment. Pray specifically for the grace to love in the moments when love is hardest.

title: Walking in Newness of Life
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 11
description: Walking in Newness of Life
reflectionPrompt: What old patterns from your past do you still carry into your marriage? Where did they come from? | How does knowing that your 'old man is crucified with Christ' give you hope for change? | What 'newness of life' do you want to see in your marriage? What specific new pattern do you want to build?
prayerFocus: Ask God for resurrection power in your marriage. Pray that old, destructive patterns would truly die and that new, Christ-honoring patterns would take their place. Thank God that in Christ, you are new creations.

title: A Surrendered Marriage
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 12
description: A Surrendered Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Are there areas of your marriage where you are yielding to selfishness rather than to God? | What does it mean practically to present your words, attitudes, and actions to God each morning? | How does remembering you are 'alive from the dead' change the way you approach surrender?
prayerFocus: Present your marriage to God as a living offering. Surrender your plans, your expectations, your rights, and your future to His lordship. Ask Him to use your marriage as an instrument of righteousness for His kingdom.

title: Patience with Each Other's Battles
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 13
description: Patience with Each Other's Battles
reflectionPrompt: What is the recurring struggle your spouse faces that tests your patience the most? How does Romans 7 change your perspective on it? | Do you believe your spouse genuinely wants to change? How does that belief (or lack of it) affect your attitude toward them? | How can you be a companion in your spouse's battle against sin rather than a critic on the sidelines?
prayerFocus: Pray for patience with each other's battles. Confess any impatience or contempt you have harbored. Ask God to give you eyes to see your spouse as a fellow soldier and to fight alongside them with grace.

title: Who Shall Deliver Us?
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 14
description: Who Shall Deliver Us?
reflectionPrompt: Is there an area of your marriage where you have been trying to 'deliver yourselves' by your own effort? How is that working? | What does it look like to move from self-reliance to Christ-dependence in your marriage? | How does Paul's immediate transition from 'wretched man' to 'I thank God' give you hope tonight?
prayerFocus: Cry out to God together for deliverance — from destructive patterns, from recurring sin, from the weight of your own limitations. Then thank Him through Jesus Christ, who is your deliverer. Rest in His ability, not your own.

title: No Condemnation
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 15
description: No Condemnation
reflectionPrompt: In what ways — even subtle ones — do you make your spouse feel condemned? | Do you live under self-condemnation? How does that affect your marriage? | What would your marriage look like if both of you truly believed and practiced 'no condemnation'?
prayerFocus: Thank God for the glorious truth of Romans 8:1 — no condemnation in Christ. Ask Him to root out every condemning word, look, and attitude from your marriage and replace it with the freedom of the Gospel.

title: The Spirit Prays for Your Marriage
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 16
description: The Spirit Prays for Your Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Have you ever felt so burdened that you did not know how to pray for your marriage? How does this passage comfort you? | How does knowing the Spirit intercedes 'according to the will of God' change your anxiety about the future? | Do you truly believe that 'all things work together for good' for your marriage? Where is that belief tested most?
prayerFocus: Spend time in quiet prayer tonight, trusting the Spirit to intercede on your behalf. You do not need to have the right words. Simply come before God and let the Spirit pray through you with groanings that go deeper than language.

title: God Fights for Your Marriage
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 17
description: God Fights for Your Marriage
reflectionPrompt: Do you live as though God is for your marriage or against it? How does your daily attitude reflect your belief? | What is the biggest challenge your marriage faces right now? How does knowing God fights for you change your perspective? | If God gave His Son for you, what lesser thing could He possibly withhold from your marriage?
prayerFocus: Declare together: God is for us. Pray boldly and confidently, knowing that the One who gave His Son will freely give you everything your marriage needs. Fight from victory, not toward it — the battle is already won.

title: Unbreakable Covenant Love
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 18
description: Unbreakable Covenant Love
reflectionPrompt: What forces have been trying to separate you from each other? How can you face them together with Romans 8:35-39? | What does it mean to be 'more than conquerors' in your marriage? How is that different from barely surviving? | How does Christ's unbreakable love for you empower you to love each other with unbreakable commitment?
prayerFocus: Pray Romans 8:35-39 over your marriage. Declare that nothing will separate you from each other or from the love of Christ. Ask God to make your covenant love as firm and unshakable as His.

title: Depending on God's Mercy
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 19
description: Depending on God's Mercy
reflectionPrompt: Have you been trying to fix your marriage by willpower alone? Where has that approach fallen short? | What does it mean practically to depend on God's mercy in your marriage rather than your own effort? | How can you continue to work hard at your marriage while simultaneously resting in God's mercy?
prayerFocus: Confess together your inability to sustain your marriage by your own strength. Ask for God's mercy — His undeserved, supernatural intervention — to do in your marriage what your willing and running cannot accomplish.

title: Speaking Truth in Your Home
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 20
description: Speaking Truth in Your Home
reflectionPrompt: Are you better at believing in your heart or confessing with your mouth? Where do you need to grow? | What truth about your spouse have you been carrying in your heart but not expressing? | Is your home a place where truth is welcomed or feared? What can you do to make it safer for honesty?
prayerFocus: Pray for the courage to speak truth in your home — truth of affirmation, truth of confession, and truth of honesty. Ask God to align your hearts and your mouths so that what you believe is freely spoken.

title: Worshiping Together at God's Wisdom
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 21
description: Worshiping Together at God's Wisdom
reflectionPrompt: How often do you and your spouse worship together outside of church? What holds you back? | Is there a situation in your marriage where you need to trust God's unsearchable wisdom rather than demanding answers? | What would change in your marriage if you truly embraced that 'of Him, and through Him, and to Him are all things'?
prayerFocus: Turn your prayer time tonight into pure worship. Do not bring requests — bring praise. Marvel together at God's wisdom, knowledge, and glory. Let worship bind your hearts to each other and to Him.

title: Your Marriage as a Living Sacrifice
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 22
description: Your Marriage as a Living Sacrifice
reflectionPrompt: What does it look like practically for your marriage to be a 'living sacrifice' to God? | In what areas has your marriage been 'conformed to this world' rather than transformed by Scripture? | How does meditating on God's mercies (Romans 1-11) motivate you to offer your marriage as a sacrifice?
prayerFocus: Offer your marriage to God as a living sacrifice. Ask Him to protect you from worldly patterns and to transform your thinking, your priorities, and your love through the renewing of your minds by His Word.

title: Love Without Hypocrisy
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 23
description: Love Without Hypocrisy
reflectionPrompt: Where has hypocrisy crept into your marriage — places where you perform love without truly feeling it? | Which of Paul's commands in this passage do you most need to grow in as a spouse? | What does 'in honour preferring one another' look like in the daily routines of your marriage?
prayerFocus: Ask God to make your love genuine — without pretense, without performance, without hypocrisy. Pray through each phrase of Romans 12:9-13 together, asking God to make these qualities real in your marriage.

title: Overcoming Evil with Good
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 24
description: Overcoming Evil with Good
reflectionPrompt: What is your default response when your spouse hurts you: retaliation, withdrawal, or scorekeeping? How can you change? | What would it look like to 'overcome evil with good' in your specific marriage conflicts? | Is there an unresolved conflict between you that needs a fresh infusion of grace tonight?
prayerFocus: Pray for the supernatural ability to overcome evil with good in your marriage. Ask God to break the cycle of retaliation and replace it with the cycle of grace. Pray for peace — true, lasting peace — in your home.

title: Owe Nothing but Love
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 25
description: Owe Nothing but Love
reflectionPrompt: In what ways have you been keeping a 'ledger' in your marriage — tracking debts and credits? | If love is the only debt you owe, how does that simplify the way you approach your marriage? | Ask your spouse tonight: 'How can I love you better?' and commit to following through.
prayerFocus: Ask God to fill your marriage with love — the kind that keeps no record of wrongs, that gives without expecting return, and that never runs out. Pray that love would be the currency of your home.

title: Wake Up and Put On Christ
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 26
description: Wake Up and Put On Christ
reflectionPrompt: Would you describe the current spiritual state of your marriage as awake or asleep? Why? | What 'works of darkness' need to be cast off in your marriage? What 'armor of light' needs to be put on? | What does it mean practically for your marriage to 'put on the Lord Jesus Christ' today?
prayerFocus: Ask God to wake your marriage up spiritually. Pray for fresh urgency, fresh devotion, and fresh commitment to putting on Christ in every area of your shared life. The day is at hand — live like it.

title: Receiving One Another
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 27
description: Receiving One Another
reflectionPrompt: What differences between you cause the most conflict? Are they truly matters of principle or matters of preference? | How do you respond when your spouse's convictions or preferences differ from yours — with acceptance or with judgment? | What would change in your marriage if you truly 'received' each other without trying to change each other?
prayerFocus: Pray for the grace to receive each other fully — differences and all. Ask God to help you distinguish between biblical principles and personal preferences, and to hold your preferences loosely while holding your spouse tightly.

title: Pursuing Peace and Building Up
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 28
description: Pursuing Peace and Building Up
reflectionPrompt: Is your marriage characterized more by peace or by tension? What is one step you can take toward greater peace? | When was the last time you intentionally edified your spouse with specific encouragement? What holds you back? | What would it look like to 'follow after' peace and edification with the same energy you put into other pursuits?
prayerFocus: Pray for a marriage marked by both peace and edification. Ask God to make you peacemakers and encouragers — quick to resolve conflict and quick to build each other up.

title: Like-Minded and Welcoming
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 29
description: Like-Minded and Welcoming
reflectionPrompt: What does it mean for you and your spouse to be 'likeminded according to Christ Jesus'? Where are you already unified? Where do you need to grow? | How does the way Christ received you set the standard for how you receive your spouse? | What would change in your marriage if you received each other fresh every morning — without the weight of yesterday's failures?
prayerFocus: Pray Paul's prayer from Romans 15:5-6 over your marriage: that God would grant you to be likeminded, that you would glorify God with one mind and one mouth, and that you would receive each other as Christ has received you.

title: The Mystery Revealed
subtitle: Romans for Marriage — Day 30
description: The Mystery Revealed
reflectionPrompt: How has your understanding of marriage deepened through this month's study of Romans? | What is the single most important truth God has spoken to your marriage this month? | How do you want your marriage to display the Gospel to the world around you in the months ahead?
prayerFocus: Close with the doxology of Romans 16:25-27 prayed over your marriage: 'Now to Him who is able to establish us according to the Gospel — to God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ forever.' Dedicate your marriage to His eternal purposes and rest in His power to establish you.
